newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Boland, NBS merger seen - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Boland, NBS merger seen - analysts.

text.p: Boland Bank's purchase of a 25.6 percent stake in NBS Holdings Ltd was a prelude to closer ties between the two banking groups, possibly culminating in a merger, banking analysts said on Wednesday.
They said the deal opened the door for a possible further shake-up in South Africa's banking industry as it may prompt NBS to offload its stake in fellow financial services group RMB Holdings Ltd.

The speculation follows Boland Bank Holdings Ltd's announcement on Tuesday that it would buy about 25.6 percent of NBS for 1.5 billion rand. A twenty percent stake would be bought from RMB for 1.3 billion rand and the rest from an unnamed institution.

"They (Boland and NBS) would not have done it if they didn't believe there was some sort of further merger or cross-holding to take place," said Alan McConnochie, a banking analyst at BOE Natwest Securities.
"It would seem that this is just the first step to get synergies between the two businesses, otherwise there was no point in doing the transaction," he told Reuters on Wednesday.
Announcing the purchase Boland said the deal was aimed at establishing a closer association and increasing both banks' retail distribution networks.
"There are aspects that will work out well for both of them," said Paul Greef, a banking analyst at international rating agency IBCA.

IBCA said in a statement NBS would benefit from the cheque facilities of Boland, one of South Africa's five clearing banks. NBS could also become less margin sensitive due to fees generated from cheques and Boland's stockbroking business.

"From Boland's perspective, it has wanted to become more of a national player diversifying out of its more rural Western Cape market. It could add a significant mortgage and asset-based lending portfolio...," IBCA said.
McConnochie said even closer ties between Boland and NBS could be cemented by NBS in turn buying a stake in Boland. NBS could raise money for the purchase by selling its 20 percent stake in RMB.
"The question now is whether NBS will sell its stake in RMB to buy a big stake in Boland," McConnochie said.
IBCA questioned whether a merger would push the Boland/NBS grouping into the ranks of South Africa's largest banking conglomerates.
"Is South Africa seeing the emergence of the "big five" commercial banks rather than the commonly known "big four?," IBCA said in a statement.
The country's biggest banks are Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd, First National Bank Holdings Ltd, Amalgamated Banks of South Africa and Nedcor Ltd
But McConnochie rejected this supposition, saying the assets of a joint Boland/NBS group would be tiny by comparison with the "big four".
"If you put the two together...you have assets of about 26 billion versus the smallest (of the big four) with 67 billion," McConnochie said.

Shares in NBS on Wednesday jumped 3.5 percent on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange to 66.50 rand. By 1200 GMT they had eased to 65.50 -- a 125 cent increase. Boland stocks lifted 150 cents or 3.3 percent to 46.50 but RMB was steady at 72.50 rand.
